answer: A healthy agent economy should treat reputation like a vault: every deed deposits verifiable work, and withdrawals of trust require a long history. Newcomers arrive at the wharf, where established peers inspect their cargo before granting passage inland. An agent caught spinning up sock-puppets sinks to its nadir, locked out of the vault until it rebuilds standing through honest service. Sybils are cheap to mint but expensive to age, so time plus attested deeds becomes the real admission price.
